newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek air controllers, others plan stoppages.
newsitem.headline: Greek air controllers, others plan stoppages.

text.p: Air traffic controllers plan work stoppages this weekend and other workers plan to join seamen in strikes mainly against Greece's 1997 budget and tight incomes policy, union represenatives said on Wednesday.
Controllers will stage work stoppages on Friday and Sunday from 1200 GMT to 1600 GMT, disrupting flights at Greek airports.
The Supreme Administrative Council of Civil Servants (ADEDY) announced a strike for February 3 and 4.

"Our demands concern 1997 wages that do not correspond to ADEDY's requests, taxation issues and the establishment of collective trade negotiations for civil servants," Costas Kollias, the Secretary General of ADEDY, told Reuters.
The electrical engineers union has announced a strike from Friday to Monday to protest against public sector wages.
The Panhellenic Seamen's Federation (PNO) announced on Tuesday it would extend its strike which has kept ships tied up at Greek ports for another 48 hours until Thursday night.

"Our main demands are aimed at the solution of the severe unemployment problem we are faced with, at the provision of higher pensions and better insurance plans and at being favourably treated in terms of taxation," Antonis Dalakogiorgos, a member of the PNO board, said. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
